scope: Provider read deadlines, Claude idle-state gating and shared usage-cache recovery; not the whole provider block
reproducedAndFixed: Both providers could submit work after their busy-wait deadline when a late read reported idle; Codex could also accept a late reply.

Stalled idle/reply reads could bypass the poll-loop timeout. A shared deadline helper now bounds reads, propagates abort to Codex RPC or the Claude read-only CLI adapter, and clears its timer. It does not interrupt remote work or retry submission.
Claude treated needs-input and unavailable as idle. Only idle now passes; needs-input waits without granting approval and unavailable rejects before endpoint creation.
Claude completion waiting could report TARGET_BUSY_TIMEOUT after submission. It now shares the remaining reply budget and reports REPLY_TIMEOUT.

A synchronously throwing injected usage adapter could leave the refresh promise latched forever in both providers. Schedule adapter execution after assigning the in-flight promise. Default adapters are async: this reproducer covers the injection contract, not a proven live outage.
The new deadline helper splits durations above Node's maximum timer delay instead of overflowing to 1ms.

oldProviderReplay.note: Only the two provider files were replaced with baseline source in an isolated copy; the newly added deadline helper remained for its own tests.

functionReview.readBeforeDeadline: Past/exact/just-before deadlines, sync and async failure, stalled reads, abort reason, late rejection, timer cleanup and long-delay chunking. Fake time makes boundary checks deterministic.
functionReview.ClaudeProvider.list/defaultRun: Signal forwarded through the real list method to an injected read-only CLI runner; no live CLI process was aborted during verification.
functionReview.ClaudeProvider.#waitUntilIdle: Strict idle, approval waiting, unavailable/missing targets, decoys, current socket selection, bounded backoff and one progress event per phase. list identity invariant is id=claude:sessionId.
functionReview.ClaudeProvider.ask: Pre-submit deadline, no duplicate send, reply budget shared with completion, approval-to-idle transitions and endpoint finally-stop. Native final-answer provenance remains outside this block.
functionReview.CodexProvider.ask: Late idle/reply rejection and stalled thread/read, thread/items/list and thread/turns/list. Abort only the local request, close the client, no interrupt/archive/resend. Existing matching-turn and completion tests also rerun.
functionReview.Both #refreshUsage methods: Exact cache-expiry boundary, synchronous exception recovery, shared in-flight requests, negative caching and preservation of last-good value/observedAt after rejected or invalid refreshes. Refresh frequency remains unchanged.

finalTreeReplay.timeoutReview: ID 60 replaces the entire body of while(true) with an empty block. This is a non-yielding infinite loop, stopped by the process ceiling and reported separately from assertions/test deadlines.

survivorReview.reason: At exactly the maximum Node timer duration, >= adds one zero-delay scheduling hop before abort. Late results still reject; this is a timer-granularity difference, not universally equivalent.

Discovered id is derived from sessionId, so both equalities agree for valid bridge inputs. Arbitrarily inconsistent injected session objects are outside this equivalence claim.

limitations: The deadlines cover idle/reply reads, not the entire CLI command: discovery, connection/initialization, submission acknowledgement and endpoint shutdown have separate remaining review boundaries.
No native agent session, daemon, user configuration or actual credentials were modified; remote agent behavior and Claude final-answer provenance are not proven by these mocks.
Response pagination, peer receive/shutdown and usage transport/authentication/parser failures remain in TODO.md. Usage-cache recovery here assumes the reader eventually settles.
The benchmark measures in-memory processing only, not provider/TUI latency.
This is a selected mutation scope, not a provider-wide reliability score. Hash, dependency, environment or configuration changes require reassessment; tests are not frozen.
